rules.name: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) Completeness
rules.description: The project must maintain a complete, accurate inventory (SBOM) of all first-party and third-party components, including transitive dependencies, to detect unauthorized or unexpected additions.

rules.name: Component Metadata Accuracy
rules.description: Component metadata (name, version, publisher, license) must be verified against authoritative registries to detect spoofed or misrepresented packages.

rules.name: Known Vulnerability Scanning
rules.description: All components must be scanned against known-vulnerability databases before and during use, to detect components with disclosed security issues.

rules.name: Malicious Package Detection
rules.description: Components must be screened for known-malicious behavior (not just disclosed CVEs), since supply-chain attacks frequently use packages with no formal vulnerability record.

rules.name: Build Provenance Verification
rules.description: The origin and build process of a component must be verifiable and attributable to a specific, trusted source repository and build system.

rules.name: Publisher Identity Verification
rules.description: The identity of the package publisher must be verified (e.g., via signed commits or verified maintainer accounts) to reduce risk of account takeover or impersonation.

rules.name: Pedigree and Modification History
rules.description: Components that have been modified from their original upstream source must be flagged and their modification history tracked, since undisclosed modifications are a common malware insertion vector.

rules.name: Internal Fork Tracking
rules.description: Internally maintained forks of open-source components must be tracked and periodically reconciled against upstream to detect drift that could mask injected malicious changes.

rules.name: Package Manager Trust Boundary Enforcement
rules.description: Package managers must be configured to prefer trusted internal registries over public ones for internally-named packages, mitigating dependency confusion attacks.

rules.name: Install-Time Script Restriction
rules.description: Arbitrary code execution during package installation (e.g. setup.py, npm postinstall scripts) should be restricted or sandboxed, since this is a primary delivery mechanism for supply-chain malware.

rules.name: Immutable Version Pinning
rules.description: Dependencies should be pinned to specific, hash-verified versions rather than floating version ranges, preventing silent injection of a compromised newer release.
